I want to design a simple architecture for the Support Ticket Management System.

The agreed stack is:

Backend:
- Java 21
- Spring Boot
- REST API
- PostgreSQL for the application
- H2 for tests where practical

Frontend:
- React + Vite

Repository:
backend/
frontend/
spec/
docs/

The application needs:
- ticket creation
- ticket listing
- ticket details
- field updates
- assignee changes
- comments
- keyword search
- status filtering
- backend-enforced status transitions
- validation
- meaningful API errors
- persistence

The backend state machine is:

OPEN -> IN_PROGRESS
IN_PROGRESS -> RESOLVED
RESOLVED -> CLOSED
OPEN -> CANCELLED
IN_PROGRESS -> CANCELLED

All other status transitions are invalid.

Please design the architecture before writing code.

Cover:

1. High-level architecture
2. Backend layers and responsibilities
3. Frontend structure
4. Communication between frontend and backend
5. Database and persistence approach
6. Where the state-machine logic belongs and why
7. Error-handling flow
8. Testing boundaries
9. Configuration and secret handling
10. Repository structure

Keep this intentionally simple. This is a small assignment, so don't introduce microservices, authentication, event buses, CQRS, Kafka, Redis, or other infrastructure that isn't required.

First show me the proposed architecture.

The architecture proposal must draw from the assignment requirements, Cursor rules, and locked decisions. The repository currently lacks spec/ and docs/ directories. I will review the locked decisions for contradictions before outlining the ten architectural topics.

The architecture will be a single monolith backend and SPA frontend. No microservices or extra infrastructure will be introduced.

Controllers will stay thin. Services will own all business rules. Repositories will handle persistence only.

The state machine belongs in the domain or service layer. Field updates and status transitions will use separate APIs. Errors will follow RFC 7807.

Java 21 records and sealed types will be used where appropriate. Constructor injection and @Transactional will be applied to services. DTOs will be used instead of entities.

Testing will split into unit tests for domain logic without Spring, integration tests for HTTP and database, and tests for every state transition. H2 will be used for tests. PostgreSQL will be used for production.

Secrets will be read from environment variables. The package layout and REST paths will follow the established conventions. A dedicated TicketStatusTransition value object in the domain layer will drive the state machine. It will be invoked by TicketService and kept out of controllers, repositories, and the frontend. The database layer will use Spring Data JPA with Flyway for schema migrations.

The database schema will contain two tables: Ticket and Comment. Tickets will store id, title, description, priority, assignee, status, and timestamps. Comments will link to tickets via foreign key and include body and timestamps. Timestamps are required by the decision and useful for audit trails.

The frontend will be a Vite React SPA with components for listing, detail, creation, and forms. An API client module will handle HTTP calls. Vite will proxy requests to the backend during development.

Communication will use JSON REST APIs. CORS or a Vite proxy will bridge the frontend and backend. WebSockets are excluded.

Integration tests will use @SpringBootTest with MockMvc against H2. They will cover ticket creation, retrieval, status transitions, and 404 and 409 responses. Unit tests will target the status machine and TicketService. Frontend tests are not required for this assignment.

Configuration will live in application.yml. Datasource credentials will come from environment variables. A .env.example file will list variables without secrets. Passwords will never be committed.

The response will present the full architecture as a design document.

Implementation details such as UUID versus Long identifiers and Flyway versus Liquibase will be framed as proposed choices rather than product requirements. The REST endpoint sketch will follow standard conventions: POST /api/v1/tickets returns 201 with a Location header; GET supports keyword and status filters; PATCH handles field updates; and status transitions will use a path-based endpoint without RPC-style verbs.

Comment operations will use POST /api/v1/tickets/{id}/comments. Comments will be embedded within ticket GET responses rather than fetched separately.

**Proposed architecture** (design only — no files or application code). Source of truth: the assignment, the locked decisions from the requirements session, and `.cursor/rules/` (layering, REST, tests, docs). `spec/` and `docs/` are not in the repo yet; those decisions are treated as agreed, not invented here.

Locked product rules (no conflict with the assignment, no extra platform): closed 5-edge state machine; create always `OPEN`; field updates vs dedicated status change; Postgres + H2 tests; React + Vite; one repo with independently runnable `backend/` and `frontend/`. No auth, users, Kafka, Redis, CQRS, or microservices.

---

## 1. High-level architecture

One **modular monolith** and one **SPA**, same git repo, two processes.

```
Browser (React + Vite)
        │  HTTPS/HTTP JSON
        ▼
Spring Boot (Java 21)  ──REST──►  PostgreSQL
        │
        └── tests use H2 (where practical)
```

- **Frontend:** create/list/detail/update/assignee/comments/search/filter; show API errors. It may hide illegal statuses as UX, but **must not** be the rule owner.
- **Backend:** validation, persistence, and the **only** status machine.
- **Dev:** Vite proxy to the API so the UI does not hard-code secrets or messy CORS for local work.
- **Run:** `backend` and `frontend` start separately.

---

## 2. Backend layers and responsibilities

Classic Spring layering, matching `java-springboot.md`.

| Layer | Responsibility | Must not |
|--------|----------------|----------|
| **Controller** | Map `/api/v1/...`, `@Valid` request DTOs, call **one** service method, return response DTOs, `201` + `Location` on create | Status machine, JPA, assignment rules |
| **Application/service** | Use cases: create, list/search/filter, get, update fields, change status, add comment. `@Transactional` here. Map entity ↔ DTO | HTTP types, SQL in controllers |
| **Domain** | `TicketStatus` enum, **transition policy** (allowed edges only), domain exceptions | Persistence annotations on API types |
| **Repository** | Load/save/query (`ILIKE` title/description, filter by status) | “Is this transition allowed?” |
| **Exception handler** | Map exceptions → one Problem Details JSON | Swallow errors or return `200` with an error body |

**Suggested packages (single module):**  
`api` (controllers, DTOs, exception handler) → `application` (services) → `domain` (ticket, status, transitions, exceptions) → `persistence` (JPA entities, Spring Data repos).

**Use cases (one service is enough):** create ticket; list with optional keyword + single status; get by id (ticket + comments); patch fields (title, description, priority, assignee only); transition status; add comment.

Java 21 records for DTOs; enums for `TicketStatus` and `Priority` (`LOW`/`MEDIUM`/`HIGH`). Constructor injection; no field `@Autowired`.

---

## 3. Frontend structure

Simple Vite + React app, no Next.js, no global state library unless it becomes necessary.

```
frontend/src/
  api/          HTTP client (tickets, comments, errors)
  pages/        list, create, detail
  components/   ticket form, comment list/form, status control, error display
  types/        mirrors API DTOs
```

**Screens (acceptance criteria only):**

1. **List** — keyword + status filter, results, link to detail, link to create  
2. **Create** — title, description, priority; no status field  
3. **Detail** — fields, assignee, comments, status action, errors  

Status control should offer only the five legal next states **as UX**, still handle `409` if the server rejects. Assignee is a free-text optional string (no user picker).

---

## 4. Communication between frontend and backend

JSON REST, versioned paths from `api-standards.md`. No RPC verbs (`/updateStatus`).

| Capability | Proposed contract |
|------------|-------------------|
| Create | `POST /api/v1/tickets` → **201** + `Location` |
| List / search / filter | `GET /api/v1/tickets?keyword=&status=` |
| Details | `GET /api/v1/tickets/{id}` (include comments) |
| Field update | `PATCH /api/v1/tickets/{id}` — title, description, priority, assignee only; **no status** |
| Status | `PATCH /api/v1/tickets/{id}/status` with `{ "status": "IN_PROGRESS" }` (sub-resource, not a verb) |
| Comment | `POST /api/v1/tickets/{id}/comments` |

Invalid `status` query → **400**, not an empty list. Unknown id → **404**. Illegal transition → **409**, ticket unchanged.

No WebSockets, JWT, or API gateway.

---

## 5. Database and persistence

**App:** PostgreSQL. **Tests:** H2 where practical. Data must survive restart (real DB, not in-memory for the running app).

**Tables (minimal):**

- **ticket:** id, title, description, priority, assignee (nullable), status, created_at, updated_at  
- **comment:** id, ticket_id (FK), body, created_at  

No users table. Comments are rows, not a blob (multiple comments).

**Approach:** Spring Data JPA + a small schema-migration tool (Flyway is enough). Repositories: find by id; list with optional status and case-insensitive title/description match; save ticket/comment.

IDs: server-generated (`BIGINT` identity or UUID — implementation detail, not a product rule).

---

## 6. Where the state machine belongs and why

**Belongs in the domain**, invoked from the ticket service, e.g. a small `TicketStatusTransitions` (or equivalent) with the closed set:

- `OPEN → IN_PROGRESS | CANCELLED`  
- `IN_PROGRESS → RESOLVED | CANCELLED`  
- `RESOLVED → CLOSED`  
- everything else, including **same-status**, **rejected**

**Why:**

- Project rule: backend owns rules; controllers/repos/UI do not.  
- One place to unit-test every allowed and rejected pair without Spring.  
- Service loads ticket, asks the policy, persists only if allowed; illegal → `IllegalTicketTransitionException`, transaction rolls back, **no partial update**.  
- Create **sets `OPEN` in the service**; create DTO has no status field.

The UI may filter buttons; that is not enforcement.

---

## 7. Error-handling flow

```
Jakarta Validation on DTO
        │ fail → 400 + field errors
        ▼
Service / domain
        │ TicketNotFoundException → 404
        │ IllegalTicketTransitionException → 409
        │   detail: current, attempted, not allowed
        │ other validation (blank after trim, etc.) → 400
        ▼
@RestControllerAdvice → RFC 7807: type, title, status, detail, instance
```

- Do not use **500** for expected domain failures.  
- No stack traces, SQL, or persistence internals in JSON.  
- Do **not** implement **401/403** (no auth).  
- Frontend maps `detail` / field errors to the screen.

Illegal transition: reject the **whole** status operation; no status write.

---

## 8. Testing boundaries

Per `testing.md`: behaviour and the **full** matrix, not line coverage.

| Boundary | What | How |
|----------|------|-----|
| **Domain unit** | Every allowed edge; every rejected pair (incl. same-status); create status not client-driven | No Spring context; call domain/service API, **not** “set field and save” |
| **Service unit** | Field update does not change status; comment on CLOSED/CANCELLED allowed; search+filter together | Mock repository if useful |
| **API + DB integration** | Create, get, persist transition, 404, 400 invalid filter, 409 illegal transition + error shape | Spring test + **H2**; assert HTTP **and** Problem Details |
| **Frontend** | Optional later; not required to prove the machine | Manual/acceptance against running API |

Controller-only smoke tests do **not** replace domain transition tests.

---

## 9. Configuration and secret handling

- Datasource URL, user, password via **environment / Spring config**, not committed.  
- `application.yml` (or equivalent) with placeholders; local/dev overrides gitignored.  
- Document **names** of variables in README/`docs`, never real passwords.  
- H2 settings in **test** profile only.  
- No API keys in the frontend bundle beyond a public base URL (dev proxy preferred).

---

## 10. Repository structure

```
backend/          Spring Boot app (independently runnable)
frontend/         React + Vite (independently runnable)
spec/             product/API/architecture specs (to be written later)
docs/             docs/decisions/ for durable decisions
.cursor/rules/    already present
README.md         pointer to docs, how to run (no duplicated HTTP tables)
```

Keep specs and ADRs aligned when status set, paths, or error codes change. Chat is not the long-term source of truth; after this phase, architecture belongs in `spec/` / `docs/decisions/` — **not in this reply as file writes**.

---

## Explicitly out of this design

Auth, roles, user directory, notifications, attachments, SLA, pagination, audit log, event bus, Redis, Kafka, CQRS, API gateway, comment edit/delete, searching comments, skipping or reopening statuses, client-chosen create status.

---

## Implementation choices (not extra product rules)

These are proposed so we can spec later without pretending the assignment required them:

- `PATCH .../status` sub-resource rather than embedding status on field PATCH  
- Comments nested under ticket details GET  
- Flyway + JPA  
- Vite proxy in development  
- RFC 7807 as already in project API rules  

If this architecture is acceptable, next step is writing it into `spec/` and `docs/decisions/` — still without application code, when you ask.
